newsitem.title: CHINA: Smaller HK banks up on hopes of China partnerships.
newsitem.headline: Smaller HK banks up on hopes of China partnerships.

text.p: Shares of smaller Hong Kong banks rose as investors sought out possible acquisition targets of mainland companies following a possible deal involving of Liu Chong Hing Bank Ltd, brokers said on Friday.

"Rumours surrounding Liu Chong Hing Bank fueled anticipation that other smaller banks might also be targets, and that their outlook could be boosted if Chinese interests did take stakes in them," said Jason Tang, sales manager at South China Brokerage.
Liu Chong Hing Bank said it was in talks with several parties including China's COSCO group regarding a possible capital injection into the bank.
Brokers said there were rumours that COSCO (Hong Kong) Group Ltd, the parent of COSCO Pacific Ltd, might increase its stake in Liu Chong Hing bank from the current five percent.
Trading in shares of Liu Chong Hing Bank, parent Liu Chong Hing Investment Ltd, and COSCO Pacific have been suspended pending announcements.

"China intending to slow down the pace of asset injections by red chips will encourage red chips with high PEs (price earnings mutliples) to look into local low PE companies, such as banks," said Ricky Tam, senior analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
"Banks with relatively low PEs and rather steady earnings, are seen to be attractive for red chip firms," Tam added.

Shares of Wing Hang Bank surged HK$3.30 or 8.42 percent to HK$42.50 in late morning, Wing Lung Bank rose HK$1.50 to HK$49.50, Union Bank rose HK$0.75 to HK$18.60 and Kwong On Bank rose HK$0.60 to HK$13.
Giant HSBC Holdings Plc also gained in line with the smaller banks by adding HK$2.00 to HK$243, Hang Seng Bank rose HK$4.50 to HK$111.50 and Bank of East Asia also up HK$0.80 to HK$31.70.
